  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k3 ===
- File: scripts/security_audit.sh
  Line or code reference: line 110, `rm -f -- "${writable_probe_path}"` inside `security_audit_require_writable_destination` (lines 104-111)
  Problem: The probe cleanup is a bare command under `set -euo pipefail` (line 4) with no failure handling. All five call sites (lines 300, 484, 485, 526, 527) invoke the function as a bare command, so errexit is active. If `rm` exits non-zero after `mktemp` succeeded (filesystem remounted read-only or permissions changed between the two syscalls, NFS/server-side I/O error), the script aborts with a raw shell exit: the curated `security-audit: phase=... error=destination is not writable` diagnostic is never emitted, and the empty probe file persists in `${required_parent}` because it lives outside `${SECURITY_AUDIT_RUNTIME_DIR}`, which the EXIT trap at line 273 removes. The abort still fails closed before the codex run, so the preflight's core invariant (no model spend on a bad destination) is preserved; the gap is diagnostic quality plus a possible leftover artifact, contrary to the "inert, side-effect-free preflight" contract the PR itself cites.
  Why it fails at runtime: on a degraded filesystem between probe creation and deletion, the run dies with an unstructured shell error and can leave `.security-audit-writable-probe.*` behind in the operator's findings directory instead of reporting the structured preflight failure.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- File: scripts/security_audit.sh
  Line or code reference: 110, `rm -f -- "${writable_probe_path}"`
  Problem: The cleanup command is unguarded. Under `set -euo pipefail` (line 4), if `rm -f` returns non-zero on a real error (I/O error, directory permission issue, filesystem quota), the script aborts immediately without emitting the curated "destination is not writable" diagnostic that the other probe-failure branches emit.
  Why it fails at runtime: When `mktemp` succeeds but `rm -f` fails, the probe artifact remains on disk AND the script exits with a raw shell abort instead of the structured preflight failure. The PR description explicitly states the goal is "the same `destination is not writable` diagnostic" for all probe failures, but this cleanup path bypasses that contract. The Copilot review comment (entry[0]) and all five pass-1 reviewers flagged this gap. The fix is to wrap the `rm -f` in an `if !` check and emit the same diagnostic on failure, matching the other branches.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
